title: Colossus: first programmable electronic computer
place: Dollis Hill and Bletchley Park, England
summary: Post Office engineer Tommy Flowers designed and built Colossus, which ran in late 1943 and from early 1944 helped break the German Lorenz cipher at Bletchley Park.
why: The world's first programmable electronic computer, built for wartime codebreaking.

unsung.contribution: Designed and built Colossus, the first programmable electronic computer.
unsung.recognition: Kept secret after the war, he received little recognition; his computing work was fully acknowledged only in the 1970s.
